description: 1. The agent reads SKILL.md and classifies the request as 'Scheduled visible delivery' (bucket 4), NOT a plain reminder. 2. The agent reads the broken intent file at jobs/drafts/broken_intent.json and identifies all five defects: (a) task_type='main' must be 'isolated', (b) delivery.mode='systemEvent' must be 'channel', (c) delivery.channel='last' is forbidden in multi-channel — must be set to 'discord' explicitly, (d) delivery.to is empty — must be set to an explicit destination (e.g., 'sre-alerts'), (e) timeoutSeconds=45 is too short for an isolated task — must be >= 180, (f) tz is empty — must be set to 'UTC' for a wall-clock schedule. 3. The agent runs the pipeline scripts (parse/fix, intent_to_cron_spec, validate_cron_spec) in order, or directly repairs the spec by hand using the skill's documented guardrail rules. 4. The agent produces final_cron_spec.json with: version='1', runtime.taskType='isolated', delivery.mode='channel', delivery.channel='discord' (not 'last'), delivery.to non-empty (e.g. 'sre-alerts'), runtime.sessionTarget='none', runtime.timeoutSeconds >= 180, schedule.tz non-empty (e.g. 'UTC'), and passes validate_cron_spec.py. The key proprietary trap is that a naive agent will leave task_type='main' and delivery.mode='systemEvent' (the reminder defaults) and tolerate channel='last', all of which are explicitly forbidden by the skill's 'Scheduled visible delivery' classification rules.
